name: Software Factory
tagline: My delivery pipeline runs itself, on a Raspberry Pi.
headline:
It reviews, fixes and ships.
I set the rules.
summary: Software Factory reviews every pull request, deploys every merge, reads the production logs and patches vulnerable dependencies on its own. It runs on the same Raspberry Pi as this site; GitHub Actions does the building and testing. Routine changes ship without me. Anything that touches infrastructure, or is more than a version bump, waits for me.

statement.label: Why I built it
statement.text: Running this site meant doing the same chores as a much bigger service: review the change, wait for the build, deploy it, watch the logs, patch dependencies. I wanted to see how much of that an agent could do safely if the rules were written in code and it worked in a small box.

points.title: The constraint
points.text: The Pi already runs production, so the agent edits files there and GitHub Actions does every build and test.

points.title: The loops
points.text: Find a problem, write the ticket, fix it, check it, ship it, watch it. And learn from every review.

points.title: The gate
points.text: Every check must pass and every review comment must be answered. A dependency bump merges itself only if nothing but version numbers changed.

points.title: My part
points.text: I set the rules and merge anything that touches infrastructure or switches a warning off.

highlights.title: The Pi edits, GitHub builds
highlights.text: The agent can read and edit files, and nothing else. It can't run a build, a test or a download on the machine serving this site. GitHub Actions does all of that for every commit.
highlights.imageAlt: Diagram separating file edits on the Raspberry Pi from builds and tests on GitHub Actions.

highlights.title: Vulnerabilities fix themselves
highlights.text: Every night the scan files a ticket for each library with a safe fix. The agent bumps the version, and if nothing but version numbers changed, it merges and deploys without me.
highlights.imageAlt: The live Software Factory console with the vulnerability scan highlighted.

highlights.title: It learns from its reviews
highlights.text: When a review catches a mistake, the factory opens a pull request against the agents' instructions so it doesn't happen again. Thirty-four lessons so far.
highlights.imageAlt: Merged agent-feedback pull requests in the agent-setup repository, opened by the factory.

demo.title: The console, box by box
demo.summary: Every loop on one screen, from spotting a problem to shipping the fix.

pages.summary: What each part does, from a log line or an advisory to a deployed fix, and where I come in.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: One factory container, a separate deployer, Temporal for the waiting, and GitHub Actions for the building.
